approved_scope: Implement the proposed generated-asset reuse and avoid redundant whole-firmware comparison builds. Preserve required checks, features, and asset quality.
findings: tools/build.py generate() unconditionally runs gen_font.py, gen_drum_samples.py, and the custom or built-in break-bank generator.
gen_drum_samples.py produces both x0x_drum_samples.h and x0x_drum_tables.h and imports sampleio.py; its source WAVs are assets/909/{hh,ride,crash}.wav.
gen_font.py reads X0X_FONTSET and the ordered X0X_FONT_DIRS search path; resolves bundled fonts first; imports Pillow and depends on font-renderer feature availability and libraries.

gen_builtin_break.sh compiles gen_builtin_break.c and drum909.c using CC (default cc), -O2 -ffp-contract=off, generated samples/tables and transitive project/system headers, then executes the renderer.
gen_break_bank.py imports sampleio.py and reads bank.txt and selected WAVs from X0X_BREAK_BANK. The generated comment also includes the bank folder name.
Fresh validation worktrees discard build/gen. A build-directory-only cache will not remove repeated generation across validations.
The active native orchestration lane modifies dev_validate.py and validation_inputs.py, not build.py. Its worker already mounts the git common directory read-write at the same absolute path.
A cache under git-common-dir/x0x37-asset-cache can survive scratch worktrees without another Docker mount or dependency-source modification. A non-Git checkout needs a safe fallback.
No routine second Mac/Linux full firmware build is required. Cache correctness can be checked at generated-output scope. There is no permission to silently reduce font or audio quality.
requirements: Use content hashes for actual generator inputs and runtime dependencies. Do not use only mtimes or commit IDs.
Keep font, drum data, and break-bank cache keys separate so an unrelated input change does not regenerate every asset.
Include resolved selected font bytes, fontset/search semantics, Pillow/FreeType/RAQM and relevant interpreter/native-library identity; never share fonts across incompatible rendering environments.
Include sampleio.py, WAV contents, Python/math runtime dependencies for drum/sample generation. Track both output headers together.

For built-in breaks include generator scripts/C, drum909.c, transitive headers, generated drum headers, effective CC and compiler/runtime/library identities. If trustworthy dependency discovery fails, regenerate instead of guessing.
For custom banks include bank manifest, actual named WAV contents and folder-name semantics, sampleio.py and runtime. Distinguish the built-in bank.
Verify output hashes before reuse. Missing, corrupted, partial, interrupted or concurrently written cache entries must never count as hits.
Publish cache entries atomically. Validate inputs again before publication so a changed input cannot seed a stale key. Preserve failure exit codes.

Use a cache location shared by fresh worktrees, scoped to this local repository; make unavailable/unwritable cache a performance miss, never a correctness failure. Avoid cache contents becoming source/provenance inputs.
Keep existing generator output and all target/compiler/budget/package guards. No routine second whole firmware build merely for Mac/Linux comparison.

Measure cold/warm asset generation and actual reuse in a fresh scratch worktree. Test input edits with restored mtimes, generator changes, selected runtime/config changes, output corruption, failures and concurrent writers.
Test at asset scope. Do not run a complete old Linux validator simply to time a baseline already measured in build-time-audit.
Do not edit the active native validator lane or active firmware integration. Deliver a separately checked asset commit and explicit combination handoff.
not_done: No asset cache is implemented in this audit.
No asset runtime saving is claimed.
